key_insight: Charge injection from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbed CO is strongly material-dependent, with hot-electron transfer consistently exceeding hot-hole transfer because CO’s LUMO lies closer to the metal Fermi level than its HOMO.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies which nanoparticle metals are most promising for photocatalytic designs that exploit direct light-induced charge injection rather than relying on slow thermalized carriers.
method: Ab initio DFT is used to model adsorbate–metal electronic interactions for CO on metal surfaces.
A macroscopic electrodynamics model describes localized surface plasmon excitation in large spherical nanoparticles.
The combined framework is applied across nine metals: Ag, Au, Cu, Al, Ni, Rh, Pd, Ir, and Pt.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a comparative screening across nine metals, showing the largest optical-range electron injection for Al, Ag, Cu, and Au, with Cu and Au benefiting from significant plasmonic enhancement.
watch_item: The conclusions are specific to large spherical nanoparticles and CO adsorption, so transferability to other shapes, sizes, or adsorbates may require recalculation.
paper_title: Material dependence of direct light-induced charge injection from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbates
